title: Repairs are invoiced when the job is completed
rule: One DRAFT invoice is created in Xero for the final amount of the job, not the quote.
plain: Repairs are invoiced when the job is finished, for the final amount, not when the deal is won.

acceptance.given: a repair opportunity is Closed Won and the job is not complete
acceptance.then: no invoice is created

acceptance.given: the job is marked complete with a final amount
acceptance.then: one DRAFT invoice for the final amount exists in Xero

title: Deposits on large repairs
trigger: Repair won with a deposit percentage
rule: The deposit is a share of the quote and is invoiced when the deal is won. The balance is the final amount less the deposit and is invoiced on completion, so the two add up to the final amount to the penny. If the final amount is below the deposit, finance is told that a credit is due.
plain: Large repairs can be billed as a deposit first (usually half, set per job) and a balance on completion.

acceptance.given: a repair quoted at £1,001.01 with a 50 percent deposit
acceptance.then: the deposit is £500.51 and the balance is £500.50

acceptance.given: a repair quoted at £1,001.01 with a 50 percent deposit, completed at a final amount of £1,200
acceptance.then: the deposit is £500.51 and the balance is £699.49, which add up to the final amount

acceptance.given: a repair quoted at £1,000 with a 50 percent deposit, completed at a final amount of £400
acceptance.then: the balance is minus £100 and finance is told that a credit is due

title: Monthly invoices for planned maintenance
rule: A billing schedule is created at Closed Won. One DRAFT invoice per month is created in advance, from the start date, for the term, on the contract's own day of the month (pending G-17). The annual April uplift is applied from the first April after the contract starts. Every invoice has its own code: the job number, then the billing month.
plain: Planned maintenance contracts are invoiced monthly in advance for the whole term, with the April price rise applied.

acceptance.given: a 12 month contract starting 31 January at 500 a month with a 3.4 percent uplift from April
acceptance.then: the dates are 31 Jan, 28 Feb, 31 Mar, 30 Apr and so on, and the amount is 517 from April

title: Account code by type of work
rule: Planned maintenance lines carry account 200 and repairs 210. Finance can change a code before approving.
plain: The right account code is filled in for you.

acceptance.given: a planned maintenance line
acceptance.then: the account code is 200

title: VAT treatment
rule: Each job has a VAT treatment: Standard, Zero rated, Exempt or No VAT, mapped to the Xero tax types OUTPUT2, ZERORATEDOUTPUT, EXEMPTOUTPUT and NONE. It defaults to Standard. Anything marked reverse charge is held for review and never guessed.
plain: The right VAT is set on each invoice, and anything unusual is held for finance to decide.

acceptance.given: a job with no VAT treatment
acceptance.then: the tax type is OUTPUT2

acceptance.given: a job marked reverse charge
acceptance.then: no invoice is created and finance is asked

title: Regional split
rule: Every line carries the Region of the customer (North or South) as the Xero tracking category. A customer with no Region is held, not guessed.
plain: Income is split by North and South for the board pack.

acceptance.given: a South customer
acceptance.then: the Region tracking option is South

acceptance.given: a customer with no Region
acceptance.then: no invoice is created and the reason is logged

title: Purchase order number, and who is billed
rule: When the customer quotes a purchase order, the invoice Reference shows it and nothing else (the job number when there is no PO). A customer marked as needing a PO (the housing associations) with no PO on the job is held, not drafted, because they send the invoice straight back. The invoice goes to the billing contact when there is one, otherwise to the customer.
plain: Invoices show the customer's PO number and go to the right person, and an invoice for a customer who needs a PO is held if there is none.

acceptance.given: a job with PO HA-7781 and job number OPP-2210
acceptance.then: the Reference reads PO HA-7781

acceptance.given: a housing association that needs a PO and a job with none
acceptance.then: no invoice is created and finance is asked for the PO

title: Payment terms by customer
rule: The due date is the invoice date plus the customer's terms: 30 days unless the customer has 45 or 60. The invoice is dated on the day the job was completed, or on the schedule date for a monthly invoice, not on the day the sync ran.
plain: Each customer's own payment terms are used.

acceptance.given: a customer on 45 day terms
acceptance.then: the due date is 18 March 2027

acceptance.given: a job completed on 29 January 2027, with the sync running on 1 February
acceptance.then: it is dated 29 January 2027 and, on 30 day terms, due on 28 February 2027

title: Finance approves every invoice
rule: The sync only ever creates DRAFT invoices and never approves one. Approval happens in Xero by the finance manager.
plain: Nothing goes to a customer without finance seeing it.

acceptance.given: any invoice created by the sync
acceptance.then: its status is DRAFT

acceptance.given: the sync tries to approve an invoice
acceptance.then: it is refused

title: Cover when the finance manager is away
rule: A named deputy has approval rights in Xero. If the finance manager is away and no deputy is named, finance is told before drafts pile up.
plain: Someone else can approve when the finance manager is off.

acceptance.given: the finance manager is away and a deputy is named
acceptance.then: the deputy is the approver

acceptance.given: the finance manager is away and no deputy is named
acceptance.then: a warning is raised

title: Drafts appear by the end of the working day
rule: A draft invoice appears by 17:00 on the day of the trigger, or by 17:00 on the next working day if the trigger falls outside working hours (09:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday, bank holidays excluded). If the client wants a tighter target, the number changes and this check follows.
plain: A draft invoice appears by the end of the working day it was triggered, as the managing director asked.

acceptance.given: a trigger at 11:00 on a Wednesday
acceptance.when: the draft is created at 16:00 the same day
acceptance.then: the target is met

acceptance.given: a trigger at 18:00 on a Friday
acceptance.when: the draft is created at 09:30 on the Monday
acceptance.then: the target is met

acceptance.given: a trigger at 11:00 on a Wednesday
acceptance.when: the draft is created at 09:00 on the Thursday
acceptance.then: the target is missed

title: Changes after an invoice exists
trigger: Amount edited on a won deal
rule: While an invoice is a draft, the draft is updated. Once an invoice is approved it is locked, no second invoice is ever created, and a task goes to finance. The locking is per invoice, so the final amount of a repair stays editable until its balance invoice is approved. If an invoice has been paid, finance raises a credit note in Xero.
plain: If the amount changes after an invoice has gone out, finance is told and no second invoice is made.

acceptance.given: an invoice is AUTHORISED
acceptance.then: a task is created for finance and no second invoice is made

acceptance.given: a deposit invoice is approved and the balance invoice does not exist yet
acceptance.when: the final amount of the job is entered
acceptance.then: it is accepted and the balance invoice is created from it

title: Payment status in Salesforce
rule: Salesforce shows Unpaid, Part paid, Paid or Overdue for each invoice, worked out from the amounts paid and due (Xero shows an invoice as approved and awaiting payment even when part paid). It says when it was last updated, because payments appear only after bank matching.
plain: Sales can see whether a customer has paid, including part payments, before sending a new quote.

acceptance.given: an invoice of 1,200 with 600 paid and not yet due
acceptance.then: it is Part paid

title: Credit notes and voided invoices are visible
trigger: Credit note or void recorded in Xero
rule: Credit notes and voids raised in Xero show against the job in Salesforce. A void on a won deal with no replacement creates a task for finance.
plain: Sales can see credit notes and voids against the job.

acceptance.given: an invoice of 1,200 with a 200 credit note allocated
acceptance.then: the net is 1,000

title: No duplicate customers, no duplicate invoices
trigger: Invoice needs a customer, or a retry
rule: The customer is matched by the stored Xero ID, then by an email that belongs to one customer only. If several customers match, an email is shared, or a name is only similar, the invoice is held for finance to choose. A retry never creates a second invoice: every invoice has its own key (the job number, then which invoice it is: the billing month, the deposit or the balance), kept on the Salesforce invoice record with the Xero InvoiceID once known. A retry after a lost answer sends the same key, so Xero treats it as the same request; it never searches Xero and adopts a look-alike. Only one run may touch a record at a time. If Xero cannot honour the key, the invoice is held for finance.
plain: The system stops and asks rather than guess, and never bills twice.

acceptance.given: a customer whose name is similar to an existing Xero customer
acceptance.then: it is held for finance

acceptance.given: a retry after a timeout where Xero may already hold the invoice
acceptance.then: it sends the same key and no second invoice is created

acceptance.given: a job whose deposit invoice is already in Xero
acceptance.then: it has its own key and the deposit is not taken in its place

acceptance.given: a second run starts while the first is still working on the record
acceptance.then: it waits

acceptance.given: one email address shared by several Salesforce accounts
acceptance.then: it is held for finance rather than matched

title: A list of failures and a morning email
rule: Every attempt is logged (record, direction, result, message, time). Finance has a list of failures. One email goes each morning if anything failed in the last 24 hours, and none when nothing did.
plain: Finance finds out about a failure the next morning, never at month end.

acceptance.given: two failures in the last 24 hours
acceptance.then: one email is sent with a count of two

title: Who sees what
rule: Finance sees payment status, the log and can re-run a failed sync. Sales sees payment status only.
plain: Sales see payment status but never the technical errors.

acceptance.given: a sales user
acceptance.then: they see the payment status but not the log

title: A clean start
rule: Nothing dated before the chosen start month is created. Every invoice already typed into Xero for the start month or later, including an open deposit, is linked to its Salesforce record first, and nothing is created for a period that has already been invoiced. A contract already running at go-live starts its schedule from the start month, not from its original start date. Every existing Xero customer is linked to a Salesforce account first, with the doubles resolved. A full rehearsal in the sandbox against the Xero demo company passes before go-live.
plain: We pick a month, stop typing from then, and nothing is billed twice.

acceptance.given: a start month of February 2027
acceptance.when: an invoice dated 28 January 2027 is considered
acceptance.then: it is not created

acceptance.given: a 12 month contract that started on 15 November 2026 and a start month of February 2027
acceptance.then: the first draft is dated 15 February 2027 and the remaining months follow the term

acceptance.given: a February 2027 invoice already typed into Xero by hand and a start month of February 2027
acceptance.when: the sync considers the same job
acceptance.then: it is linked and no second invoice is created

title: Nothing goes missing
rule: Every deal won and every job completed that day ends up as a draft invoice, a scheduled invoice or an item on the failures list. A daily count reconciles them, and anything in none of those places is listed as missing.
plain: Nothing is lost silently: every won deal or completed job is accounted for each day.

acceptance.given: 3 deals were won today and 2 of them became drafts and 1 is on the failures list
acceptance.then: all 3 are accounted for and nothing is listed as missing

acceptance.given: a won deal that is in none of those places
acceptance.then: it is listed as missing for the finance manager

title: Month end closes with every invoice approved
trigger: The working day before the books close on the third working day
rule: On the working day before the close (the third working day after month end), and on the close itself, every invoice dated in the month that is a draft, awaiting approval or held in Salesforce (with the reason) is listed, and finance and the named deputy are told. After the close, the same list is marked late.
plain: The books close on the third working day, so finance is warned if any of the month's invoices is still waiting for approval, or is held back in Salesforce, the working day before.

acceptance.given: an invoice dated 15 January 2027 that is still a draft
acceptance.then: the close is 3 February 2027 and a warning names the invoice

acceptance.given: all of January's invoices are approved
acceptance.then: no warning is raised

acceptance.given: an invoice dated 20 January 2027 held because its PO is missing
acceptance.then: the warning lists it with the reason
